resolved_by: The Supreme Court resolved the split in United States v. Davis, 139 S. Ct. 2319 (2019), holding that the residual clause of 18 U.S.C. § 924(c)(3)(B) is unconstitutionally vague.
issue: Can the residual clause of 18 U.S.C. § 924(c)(3)(B) be saved from vagueness by reading it to require a case-specific, conduct-based inquiry instead of the categorical approach?
this_court: The Eleventh Circuit follows Davis and treats the § 924(c)(3)(B) residual clause as unconstitutional. The excerpts do not name the circuits on either side of the pre-Davis split, so no sides are listed.
quote: In doing so, the Court resolved a circuit split on the issue, rejecting the position that the residual clause of § 924(c)(3)(B) should be saved from unconstitutionality by being read to encompass a case-specific, conduct-based approach, rather than a categorical approach.
cite: In re: Michael Price, 964 F.3d 1045 (11th Cir. 2020)
